samples.summary: Read-only PDF mount still writes presence on every page change, which enforcement (now the default) refuses at PushPull
samples.evidence: `onActivePageChange` does `doc.update((_r, p) => p.set({ activePage: pageIndex }))` with no `readOnly` guard, and it is wired unconditionally into `PdfViewer` (`renderPageOverlay`/`onActivePageChange` at line 310) for both the owner and the share route. This is exactly the reasoning the diff itself applies 60 lines above to justify `initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : initialPdfRoot()}`: a local change on a read-only mount is carried by the next `PushPull`, whose verb is derived from the change pack, so it arrives as `rw` and `hasAccess()` refuses it for a share-link `viewer` (`yorkie-auth.controller.ts:322`, `link.role === 'editor'`). A presence-only change is still a change in the pack. `packages/backend/test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:513-520` records that a viewer's `sync()` carrying a local change comes back `PermissionDenied`. Before this diff that was latent (shadow mode allowed everything unless an operator opted in); with enforcement as the default, a viewer-role PDF share link that merely *scrolls* now gets its sync denied, so comments stop flowing for it. The seed was fixed and the presence write in the same file was not.

samples.summary: Slides (and board) viewer mounts publish presence on navigation/selection — the same denied-PushPull path the diff closed for notes
samples.evidence: `broadcast()` calls `store.updatePresence({ activeSlideId, selectedElementIds, selectedTableCells })` and is subscribed to `editor.onCurrentSlideChange` / `onSelectionChange` / `onCellSelectionChange` (lines 1149-1151) with no `readOnly` gate, so a viewer-role share link changing slides emits a presence-only local change. `packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:593-597` has the same unguarded `store.updatePresence` on selection change (only the *cursor* publisher is gated by `if (!readOnly)` at line 538). By the diff's own argument (`pdf-collab.tsx:191-201`, `read-only.ts:57-67`) such a change is pushed as verb `rw` and refused for a viewer, and the notes path was deliberately neutered (`readOnlyNoteStore` covers `setLocalSelection`) for precisely this reason. Making enforcement the default turns these into live denials on any deployment that registered `PushPull`. Confidence is low only because I could not confirm from the repo whether a read-only slides/board mount actually emits those callbacks.

samples.summary: Divider drag ignores where inside the 25px band the pointer grabbed, so the divider offsets from the cursor by up to its own width
samples.evidence: `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth` then `ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track` makes the editor pane's final width exactly `clientX - rect.left`, i.e. the divider's *left edge* lands on the pointer regardless of where in the 25px band the drag started. The painted hairline is centred (12px padding each side), so it sits ~12.5px right of the cursor and the band visibly jumps on the first `pointermove`. The old code divided by `rect.width` while the pane still shrank to `ratio * (rect.width - 7)`, which incidentally put the hairline within ~3.5px of the pointer — so widening the band to 25px without subtracting the grab offset (`e.clientX - divider.getBoundingClientRect().left`) makes tracking worse, not "exact" as the new comment claims.

samples.summary: `track` can be 0, producing NaN pane widths
samples.evidence: `track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth` is 0 when the container is exactly as wide as the divider (25px) and negative when narrower. `ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track` is then ±Infinity or, when the pointer is exactly at `rect.left`, `0/0 = NaN`; `Math.max(0.15, Math.min(0.85, NaN))` is `NaN`, so `flex: 1 1 NaN%` is written and silently ignored, leaving the panes stuck. Previously the divisor was `rect.width`, which is only 0 in a fully collapsed container. Degenerate layout, so contained — but the guard (`if (track <= 0) return`) is absent.

samples.summary: Share-link editor gets no feedback when an image upload fails: the uploader rejects where the notes engine's contract expects `null` after the host reported it
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` is typed `DocsImageUpload = (file: File) => Promise<string>` (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:15,40`) and *throws* on a failed request. The notes engine's `UploadImage` contract is "resolve with `null` if the upload failed and was already reported to the user" (`packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:26`), and `beginUpload` handles a rejection by `console.error` + dropping the ghost placeholder (lines 179-199). So an anonymous editor whose upload fails (oversized file, 4xx, network) sees the placeholder vanish with no toast and no image. The workspace route wraps the same operation to catch, toast and return `null` (`notes-detail.tsx:208-228`); this new mount passes the raw rejecting uploader straight through.

samples.summary: A guarded store handle throws on stringification, and `isExtensible` lies about a non-extensible target
samples.evidence: `get` maps every non-allowlisted function to `noop`, which includes the inherited `toString` and `valueOf`, while `getPrototypeOf: () => null` removes the fallback chain. `String(store)` / `` `${store}` `` therefore finds no primitive conversion and throws `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value` — a crash reachable from any future log line or error message that interpolates the handle (the raw store stringifies fine, so it only fires on viewer mounts). Separately, `isExtensible: () => true` (line 155) is a proxy invariant violation if the target is ever non-extensible: `Object.isExtensible(handle)` would throw. Both are contained, but they are behaviours the wrapper introduces rather than inherits.

samples.summary: `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` is cast to `ms.StringValue` unvalidated, so a bad value fails inside the injector at attach time instead of at startup
samples.evidence: `expiresIn: string = process.env.YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN ?? '10m'` is cast with `expiresIn as ms.StringValue` at line 86, and `YorkieService` does the same (`yorkie.service.ts:50-55`). `??` does not catch the empty string, and a numeric-looking value like `15` parses as 15 *milliseconds*. Either way the failure surfaces as a throw from `jwt.sign` inside `authTokenInjector`, i.e. inside the Yorkie SDK's auth/refresh path during a migration or a v1 request, rather than as a startup error — a token that expires instantly also produces an endless 401/refresh loop rather than a clear failure. Same latent pattern exists in `AuthService`, so this is an extension of it rather than new, but the new callers are batch scripts where a mid-run failure costs more.

samples.summary: Docs package still documents the old shadow-mode default that this change inverted
samples.evidence: The comment states the auth webhook "ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one" — the exact claim the diff corrected in `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:57-67`. `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413` carries the same stale statement. Neither is checked by any lane (nested design docs and package comments are unchecked), so a reader of the docs package now gets the opposite of the deployed default.

verdict.reason: The described code exists exactly as claimed and is reachable. `pdf-collab.tsx:124-128` writes presence via `doc.update((_r, p) => p.set({ activePage: pageIndex }))` with no `readOnly` guard, despite `readOnly` being in scope in the same component (line 92/136). It is wired unconditionally at `pdf-collab.tsx:310` and fired on scroll by `pdf-viewer.tsx:183`. The read-only viewer mount is live on the share route (`shared-document.tsx:699,707-712`, entered at 915-927). The refusal mechanism is the diff's own stated reasoning (`pdf-collab.tsx:191-202`) plus the backend: `PushPull` is not in `READ_GATED_METHODS` (`yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108`), `needWrite` follows the pack-derived verb (line 284-286), and `hasAccess` refuses a `viewer` write (line 322), with enforcement now the default (lines 120-142, 158-161). The e2e test at `revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:513-520` shows a viewer's local-change sync returning PermissionDenied. The only unproven link — whether a presence-only change counts toward the server's `pack.HasChanges()` — is flagged as unverified by the repo itself (`docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md:76-85`), which is uncertainty, not refutation. No guard exists on any path that would prevent the presence write on a read-only PDF mount.

By the diff's own argument (`pdf-collab.tsx:191-201`, `read-only.ts:57-67`) such a change is pushed as verb `rw` and refused for a viewer, and the notes path was deliberately neutered (`readOnlyNoteStore` covers `setLocalSelection`) for precisely this reason. Making enforcement the default turns these into live denials on any deployment that registered `PushPull`. Confidence is low only because I could not confirm from the repo whether a read-only slides/board mount actually emits those callbacks.

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists verbatim and is unguarded: slides-view.tsx:1129-1151 registers broadcast() (which calls store.updatePresence with activeSlideId/selectedElementIds/selectedTableCells) on onSelectionChange/onCurrentSlideChange/onCellSelectionChange with no readOnlyMount gate, despite readOnlyMount being computed at :198 and used elsewhere in the same effect; board-view.tsx:593-597 has the same unguarded updatePresence on selection change while the cursor publisher IS gated at :538. The path is reachable on a viewer mount: shared-document.tsx:384,397 and :411,423 pass readOnly = role === 'viewer'; editor.ts:1123-1125 only skips input bindings, setCurrentSlide still notifies listeners (editor.ts:1582-1595), and thumbnail-panel.ts:513 calls editor.setCurrentSlide OUTSIDE the `if (!readOnly)` block at :520 — so a viewer clicking a thumbnail emits a presence-only doc.update (yorkie-slides-store.ts:2748-2752; yorkie-board-store.ts:563-569 has no read-only check either). No readOnlySlidesStore/readOnlyBoardStore wrapper exists (only readOnlyNoteStore/readOnlyDocStore), so nothing neuters these writes the way notes/src/store/read-only.ts:137-144 deliberately neuters setLocalSelection. The consequence chain is supported by the repo: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:92-108,281-287 (PushPull is the real verb-derived gate) and pdf-collab.tsx:191-201 (a local change on a viewer mount rides the next PushPull as rw and is refused). The one open question — whether a presence-only pack satisfies the Go server's pack.HasChanges() — is explicitly recorded as unverified in docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md:76-85, which is uncertainty that keeps the finding rather than refuting it. No refutation ground applies: code present, no upstream guard, and a missing read-only guard causing denied sync / inconsistent state on a normal viewer path is in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: Read-gating AttachDocument makes the shared-PDF viewer's unconditional `initialRoot` seed an actual write by a viewer (the role-conditional seeding fix missed the PDF provider)
finding.evidence: `READ_GATED_METHODS` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:104, checkAttribute:280-282) now authorizes `AttachDocument` as a read, so a share-link *viewer*'s attach is allowed. `PdfCollabProvider` passes `initialRoot={initialPdfRoot()}` (= `{ comments: {} }`, packages/frontend/src/types/pdf-document.ts:14) unconditionally, including on the shared route where `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (shared-document.tsx:699-709). The Yorkie SDK writes every absent `initialRoot` key inside `attach`, which is precisely why the PR made every other shared provider role-conditional (`docsInitialRootForRole`, `notesInitialRootForRole`, `boardInitialRootForRole`, `sheetsInitialRootForRole`, shared-document.tsx:974-1020, with tests asserting 'seeds nothing for a viewer'). PDF was not converted, so a viewer opening a never-commented shared PDF now creates `comments` on the document — a write from the one role that must not make them, and exactly the invariant this delta's own comments claim only a hand-rolled client can break. If instead the SDK defers that seed to the next sync, the viewer's `PushPull` carries verb `rw` and is 403'd, leaving the shared PDF viewer in a permission-denied sync loop; either branch is a defect on a normally reachable path.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts `PdfCollabProvider` passes `initialRoot={initialPdfRoot()}` unconditionally, leaving the PDF provider unconverted while the other shared providers were made role-conditional. That is not the code in this tree: packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:202 reads `initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : initialPdfRoot()}`, with an explanatory comment at :191-201 citing the very same rule ("Same rule as `docsInitialRootForRole` and its siblings"). The shared route derives `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (shared-document.tsx:699) and passes it into `PdfCollabProvider` (shared-document.tsx:707-711), so a share-link viewer seeds `{}` — no `comments` write and no `rw` PushPull, so neither branch of the claimed defect is reachable. Dedicated tests assert both halves (tests/app/files/pdf-collab-provider.test.tsx:74-80: "seeds nothing on a read-only mount" -> `{}`; writable mount -> `{ comments: {} }`). The backend half of the evidence is accurate (READ_GATED_METHODS at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108 and the verb expression at :286), but the frontend precondition the finding rests on does not exist.

finding.summary: `assertYorkieAuthEnforced`'s stated precondition (the webhook refuses a preview token's writes) no longer holds absolutely once attach is authorized as a read
finding.evidence: `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` gates the public template tier on the premise that "unless the auth webhook actually refuses that token's writes" a `previewToken` grants write access, and its concrete worry is that one edit per card returns every listing to the review queue. `previewToken` is a `viewer` share link (template.service.ts:374). With `READ_GATED_METHODS` ignoring attach's verb (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:104, 280-282), a client can carry a change pack in the attach itself — the residual the new comment acknowledges — and repeat it by detach/re-attach, so the write the gate is predicated on being refused is reachable per attach even on a fully enforcing deployment. The invariant an earlier, already-merged gate relies on is weakened by this delta and neither the gate's doc comment nor the enforcement doc reconciles it.

verdict.reason: The finding's core assertion — that "neither the gate's doc comment nor the enforcement doc reconciles" the attach-as-read residual — is contradicted by the files themselves. `template-review.ts:87-100` contains a dedicated paragraph in `assertYorkieAuthEnforced`'s doc comment that explicitly qualifies the precondition: it names `READ_GATED_METHODS` and `yorkie-auth.controller.ts`, states that attach carries `rw` unconditionally so "a client that puts its change pack in the attach itself gets that pack applied, and re-attaching repeats it," recasts the "one cheap request per card" consequence as "a hand-rolled client that re-attaches per edit rather than one request per card," and concludes "this gate is a bound on the residual, not its removal." The enforcement doc does the same and names the function: `docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:292-303` ("The residual is a change pack carried by the attach itself… Features resting on this bound it rather than close it, and say so where they assert it (the public template tier's `assertYorkieAuthEnforced`)"). `yorkie-auth.controller.ts:96-108` documents the identical residual on the constant. The reviewer's quoted premise ("unless the auth webhook actually refuses that token's writes") exists at line 65-70 but is not left absolute — it is qualified 20 lines later in the same comment. Additionally, the function's logic (`template-review.ts:104-112`) is fail-closed and correct; the complaint is about prose precision, not a logic/runtime defect, so it would fall outside the correctness rubric even if the reconciliation were missing.

finding.summary: Flipping the enforcement default to "enforce" denies viewer-role share links at attach, because AttachDocument always carries verb `rw`
finding.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced()` returns true for unset, so any deployment that registers the webhook methods and configures nothing else now honors denials. But this repo's own integration test documents the verb behaviour it collides with: packages/backend/test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:371-383 — "Deliberately omits `AttachDocument` from the registered set. Empirically … `AttachDocument` always carries verb 'rw' — even for a brand-new local `Document` object with zero local changes … Gating it as the backend README's own walkthrough suggests would deny a viewer's very first attach outright". The documented registration walkthrough (packages/backend/README.md:211, packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:573, docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201) *does* add `AttachDocument`. In `decide()` → `checkAttribute()` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:257) `verb === 'rw'` ⇒ `needWrite`, and `hasAccess()` line 293 returns `link.role === 'editor'`, so a viewer share link gets 403 on its first attach and the shared document never opens. The same hazard reaches `PushPull`: Yorkie derives the verb from `pack.HasChanges()`, and every mount pushes a change pack containing its `initialPresence` (shared-document.tsx:993 sets presence for the note mount; docs/slides/sheets/board mounts likewise), so a viewer's PushPull can also be classified `rw`. docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-283 states this exact risk is *unconfirmed* and that the mitigation is "the rollout must confirm viewer-link attach/PushPull requests actually carry verb `r` (watch the shadow logs) before flipping … =true" — this change removes that staged confirmation by making enforce the default while leaving the verb question open and the README's method list unchanged.

verdict.reason: The finding's headline mechanism (attach denied) is refuted in isolation: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108 + 284-286 read-gate AttachDocument so its unconditional `rw` never sets needWrite, the cited line :257 is the missing-attributes branch, and docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-306 now documents that mitigation rather than the "unconfirmed / watch shadow logs" text quoted. However the finding also asserts the same denial reaches PushPull for viewer share links, and that half is real and reachable: shared-document.tsx:181,283 mounts SheetView for a viewer role; sheet-view.tsx:1012 constructs YorkieStore unconditionally (readOnly is only passed to initialize() at :1017); yorkie-store.ts:86-88 then performs a post-attach `doc.update((_, p) => p.set({activeTabId}))`, a local presence change that is pushed via PushPull, whose verb Yorkie derives from pack.HasChanges() (presence-only changes count) => `rw` => hasAccess (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:318-322) returns link.role === 'editor' => 403 for a viewer, and the unacked local change persists so every later sync repeats it. Unlike notes, which is genuinely no-op'd (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:139-140), no read-only sheets store wrapper exists anywhere in packages/frontend/src. Because enforcement is now the default (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-30), a registered deployment breaks live sync for viewer share links on the sheets path. That is a core-flow break in the Correctness lane, so I cannot refute on a named ground.
